title: Steps and Programmes to Identify, Groom and Develop Promising Local Athletes
what_it_is: Steps and Programmes to Identify, Groom and Develop Promising Local Athletes

sections.label: Athlete development and support questions
sections.summary: Questions ask how government identifies and develops athletes, what support exists, and how many athletes benefited.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (a) how does the Government identify, groom and develop promising athletes to achieve success in their respective sports; (b) what are the different forms of support and assistance available to such athletes during their sporting careers; and (c) how many athletes have benefitted from such schemes in recent years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (a) what forms of support and assistance can be further enhanced to enable our national athletes to succeed in their respective sports; (b) how can world-class coaches in the respective sports be attracted and retained to coach our elite national athletes; and (c) what are the Government’s plans to enhance collaboration and partnerships with the private and people sectors to continue supporting and developing Singapore athletes.

sections.label: Public sports venues investment
sections.summary: Almost $90 million yearly over three years funded public stadiums, tracks, halls and pools, administered by SSI and NYSI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Over the last three years, we have invested an average of almost $90 million each year to develop and operate stadiums, running tracks, sports halls, pools and other venues that are accessible to the general public.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The HPS is administered by the Singapore Sport Institute, or SSI, and the National Youth Sport Institute, NYSI.

sections.label: Heat retention at Tokyo Paralympics
sections.summary: At the 2020 Tokyo Paralympic Games, an SSI sport physiologist used heat retention to regulate Pin Xiu's body temperature.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: At the 2020 Tokyo Paralympic Games, for instance, the SSI sport physiologist employed various forms of heat retention to regulate Pin Xiu’s body temperature while she was in the holding room awaiting her events and this helped her to maximise her performance outcomes at the races.

sections.label: Coach led fencers to Olympics
sections.summary: Local coach Henry Koh, a 2003 SEA Games double bronze medallist, led fencers Amita Berthier and Kiria Tikanah to their maiden Olympic Games.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Together with our own local coach Henry Koh, who was himself a double bronze medallist at the 2003 SEA Games, they recently led two of our fencers, Amita Berthier and Kiria Tikanah, to their maiden Olympic Games in Tokyo.

sections.label: Athlete funding and spexScholarship
sections.summary: Funding offsets coaching, training, competitions, equipment and sport science support; spexScholarship has gone to 168 athletes since 2013.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: There is also funding to help offset their coaching costs, participate in local and overseas training and competitions, purchase equipment and obtain additional sport medicine and sport science support if they require it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: There is, of course, a range in the amount of the financial support available, with our top athletes supported at several thousand dollars per month for those who can excel at the highest level of their sport.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The spexScholarship has been given to 168 able-bodied and para-athletes since its establishment in 2013.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: There are currently, at this point in time, 76 scholarship holders, coming from a diverse cross section of sports.

sections.label: spexEducation scheme for student-athletes
sections.summary: Set up in 2013, spexEducation helps student-athletes balance sport and studies; more than 500 have benefited.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The spexEducation scheme was set up in 2013 to help athletes meet the demands of sports and education.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: I think it is a question that many parents, many athletes ask themselves: "How do we do both well at the same time?" The scheme assists student-athletes to balance their sporting and academic pursuits by supporting them with school admissions, scholarships and also importantly, scheduling their day-to-day classes and exams around their training sessions and competitions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: More than 500 student-athletes have benefited from this scheme.

sections.label: Athletes assisted since 2013
sections.summary: Since 2013, 330 former and current athletes have been assisted through this scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Since 2013, 330 former and current athletes have been assisted through this scheme.

sections.label: Athletes using grants
sections.summary: In the last five years, some 4,000 athletes have used these grants to pursue their sporting ambitions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In the last five years, some 4,000 athletes have used these grants to pursue their sporting ambitions.

sections.label: One Team Singapore Fund
sections.summary: In 2017 the Government launched the One Team Singapore Fund, a matching grant framework encouraging private and public donations for national athletes' training and competition opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In 2017, the Government recognised this and launched the One Team Singapore Fund, which is a matching grant framework, to catalyse and encourage the support of private organisations and corporations and members of the public for our national athletes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Donations to the One Team Singapore Fund are directed towards supporting athletes in areas such as enhancing their training environment and increasing their own competition opportunities.

sections.label: Government matched donations
sections.summary: To date, the Government has matched more than $15 million of public donations since 2017, half of that period being the COVID-19 pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: To date, the Government has matched more than $15 million of donations from the public since 2017, of which in half that period, as Members would know, is the COVID-19 pandemic period.

sections.label: Government commitment to sports
sections.summary: The Government will remain committed to sports, keeping facilities, programmes and activities open and accessible to every Singaporean.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The Government will therefore remain committed to sports in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We will keep our sports facilities, programmes and activities open and accessible to every Singaporean to promote a strong sporting culture and develop a pipeline of strong sporting talent.

sections.label: Kean Yew prize money
sections.summary: The speaker understands that Kean Yew did not win any prize money from his recent championship.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: The second question; more directly, I understand that Kean Yew did not win any prize money from his recent championship.

sections.label: Prize money and organisers
sections.summary: Prize money amounts are set by organisers, and the Government keeps no part of the prize money.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: All of these, whether prize money, or otherwise, the amount is determined by organisers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But I want to assure Mr Xie that the Government retains no part of this prize money.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: It is between the athlete and the relevant NSA.

sections.label: Safety nets after retirement
sections.summary: It asks what safety net arrangements the country can offer athletes after they retire from competitive sports.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: And in many cases, it will come to "make it" or "break it" point as they go full-time for many years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So, what are the safety nets arrangements that our country can offer after they retired from competitive sports?

sections.label: spex programme support for athletes
sections.summary: The spex programme provides a curated range of support from scholarship to education, business, GLOW and TAG.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We do need to ensure that our athletes are single-minded, focused and put all their energies and devote their time and mental focus on training and eventually, also on competition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And so, the spex programme that I have mentioned – from scholarship, to education, to business, to GLOW and TAG – they provide a range of support and ensure that it is curated.

sections.label: Post-competition careers for athletes
sections.summary: Athletes can find post-competition careers in sports science, nutrition, training, physiotherapy and physiology, and more can be done on the HPS framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Broadly speaking, we also want to ensure that we take advantage of and leverage the expertise of these athletes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, they can find a post-competition career in sports science, in nutrition, in training, in physiotherapy, in physiology.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: All of these are adjunct to the sporting career and we will take opportunities as much as we can to continue to develop these adjunct areas, so that the sportsmen, the athletes themselves, can continue to serve in that capacity and, at the same time, still find a career after their playing days are over.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We agree with Ms Poh that we have come quite far on the HPS framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We have also looked at the environment and working with private stakeholders like in spexBusiness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But we agree that more can be done and we will certainly press on with ensuring that athletes remain single-minded, focused on training and ensuring that they devote as much of their time and energy possible to achieving their best outcome and not have to worry about ancillary matters.
